review_notes: I read the whole file and its definitions, then grepped the Leray directory for uses of forcedMildCurve, forcedComplexCurve and dite_eq_left. The file has no @[simp] declarations and no competing or looping rules. The only simp-interface issue I found is the missing unfolding lemmas for the two dite-defined curves. I did not run Lean, so I have not tested the suggested lemmas or checked how simp would handle the proof argument in forcedMildRHS.

findings.excerpt: if hs : 0 ≤ s then forcedMildRHS b h F s hs else 0
findings.problem: Both curves are defined by `if hs : 0 ≤ s then … else 0`. The file gives no canonical lemma, simp or otherwise, for the case `0 ≤ s`. The only related lemma is `forcedComplexCurve_fourier`, which gives the Fourier transform of the complex curve and is not tagged simp. Every user therefore unfolds the definition and rewrites with `dite_eq_left`. The same boilerplate appears in this file (`unfold forcedMildCurve` then `rw [dite_eq_left hs, …]`, and the same for `forcedComplexCurve`). It also appears in RegularisedEnergyInterval.lean, ForcedRegularisedGlobal.lean, ForcedRegMomentumRep.lean, ForcedRegularisedSolution.lean and RegularisedEnergyIntervalReal.lean. Unfolding exposes the raw `dite`, so simp cannot reduce the curve at a point known to be nonnegative. The lemma `forcedComplexCurve_fourier` has an explicit `hs : 0 ≤ s` and a clean right-hand side, but it is not tagged simp either. The missing normal form is therefore `forcedMildCurve b h F s = forcedMildRHS b h F s hs`.
findings.proposed_change: Add conditional unfolding lemmas, for example `theorem forcedMildCurve_of_nonneg (hs : 0 ≤ s) : forcedMildCurve b h F s = forcedMildRHS b h F s hs := dif_pos hs` and a matching `forcedComplexCurve_of_nonneg`. Add the matching `forcedMildCurve_of_neg` and `forcedComplexCurve_of_neg` lemmas for negative times, which give 0. Mark the nonnegative and negative versions @[simp], since simp can discharge `0 ≤ s` from hypotheses. Alternatively, mark `forcedComplexCurve_fourier` @[simp] and use `simp [forcedMildCurve_of_nonneg hs]`. Then replace the `unfold …; rw [dite_eq_left …]` pairs in the listed files with these lemmas. Keep the `dite` definitions otherwise unfolded, so nothing expands unexpectedly.
findings.benefit: Proofs about the curves would use one named rewrite instead of the repeated `unfold` plus `dite_eq_left` idiom. Callers would no longer expose the `dite` form, and the zero-for-negative-time case would be handled by simp.
